page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a cloud native instance provisioned with 64 x86_64 vCPUs and 384 GB of memory. It runs on AMD EPYC 7542 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz using KVM virtualization. The configuration yields 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it between standard general-purpose and memory-optimized resource profiles. It includes 64 physical cores with one thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The instance includes no bundled local storage, no dedicated GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote block storage and additional networking setups for public access.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture optimized for parallel execution rather than single-threaded speed. The single-core stress-ng score (744.89) falls within the bottom 10%, and the single-core Geekbench score (1155.0) ranks in the bottom 25%, reflecting the conservative 2.0 GHz clock speed of the Zen 2 generation EPYC 7542. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics perform strongly, evidenced by a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 400.83 GB/sec and a PassMark CPU score of 60,061.44, both placing in the top 25%. Instruction-set tests including PassMark CPU extended instructions (75,588.0) and encryption (66,479.27) also sit in the top 25%, bolstered by hardware AES and SHA extensions.

Memory performance shows high cached read throughput of 3,728.41 GB/sec and strong large-block write bandwidth of 90.89 GB/sec. Large-block uncached read bandwidth measures 132.51 GB/sec, falling into the middle 50%. Application-level testing reflects balanced capabilities across in-memory operations and parallel compilation, achieving 61.42 million Redis SET operations per second and a Clang compilation score of 33,214.0. LLM inference processing rates remain average for prompt processing across models, though text generation on 7B models drops to 5.64 tokens/sec due to the absence of hardware accelerators.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is driven by its high resource density, delivering 64 cores and 384 GB of RAM on shared infrastructure. While it provides substantial aggregate compute and memory per resource unit, trade-offs involve low per-thread processing speeds and reliance on networked storage. It is best suited for horizontally parallel workloads, memory-resident data caches, container clusters, batch ETL processing, and backend microservices that scale over high core counts.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a virtual server powered by 64 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs at 2.0 GHz and 384 GB of RAM, running on KVM virtualization with an x86_64 architecture. The system provides a 6.0 GB RAM-per-core ratio, featuring no integrated local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators. Synthetic and application benchmarks show modest single-thread performance alongside robust multi-threaded compute, supported by strong PassMark CPU metrics and multi-threaded decompression rates in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth remains solid with 90.89 GB/sec large-block write speeds and over 61 million Redis SET operations per second. While unsuited for latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks or GPU-bound machine learning, the high core and memory capacity make it well aligned with containerized application fleets, large in-memory databases, batch data transformation pipelines, and parallel compilation tasks.
